pages.text: "Dig here, dig there!" Kiki dug outside the burrow. Stones rolled, grass clumps scattered, roots popped up. A heap grew at the entrance. Digging was fun; tidying wasn't.
On the way for water, Kiki stepped on a sharp stone. "Ouch!" Then a rain-slick grass clump sent Kiki onto their bottom. The entrance was bumpy and jumbled.
Kiki's favorite striped pebble was missing, too. They searched stones and grass without finding it. Their tail drooped between their back legs.
Nia peered down over the burrow. "Why so sad?" Mom followed, looked around, and smiled. "Don't worry. I'll teach you some magic!"
Mom tapped the stone pile. "Leave it messy, and your feet hurt, your pebble hides, and your doorway stays bumpy!" Kiki wrinkled their nose. "An ouch-burrow!"
Mom lifted her head. "But tidy it, and your feet feel fine, your pebble appears, and the entrance is smooth! That's tidy-up magic." Kiki wanted to try.
Mom taught a song. "One, stones together! Two, grass beside the burrow! Three, keep the entrance tidy!" Kiki stacked stones beneath a rock behind the burrow. Nia pushed grass aside with their muzzle.
The last stone went under the rock. The entrance was smooth and wide! Kiki stood tall and opened their chest. "I did it!" Nia and Mom beamed.
There on the bare dirt sparkled the striped pebble! Nia spotted it first. "Over there!" Kiki hugged it in their paws. "Tidying brings lost things back!"

Now Kiki knew: tidy after playing, and feet stayed comfortable and things didn't get lost. Mom stroked Kiki's back with her muzzle; Nia lowered theirs to Kiki's head. "Our tidy-up champion! Stones together, grass beside the burrow, entrance tidy!"
